content.text: : scrape/scratch inj on corneal epithelium; MC eye inj
: inj from object, FB, dry eyes (Sjogren), entropion, contact lens
, blurred vision, photophobia (pain w/ exposure to bright light), erythema
▪︎PE often difficult w/o topical anesthetic (proparacaine) → immediate pain relief + allows exam
▪︎assess VA, pupillary reactivity + accommodation, funduscopic exam before anesthetic if possible + before fluorescein
▪︎after fluorescein: Wood lamp → ⇡uptake = epithelial defect; evert eyelid to detect retained FB
: removal of any retained FB, NSAIDs for pain
▪︎retained FB: remove by irrigation after topical anesthetic (cotton swab if visualized)
▪︎CL wearers: pseudomonal coverage → FQ (ofloxacin, cipro) or aminoglycoside (tobramycin, gentamicin)
▪︎⍉patching if FB can't be removed or CL wearer
▪︎severe pain 2/2 large abrasion: cycloplegic drops (cyclopentolate) or short course oral opioids
▪︎large epithelial defect, purulent d/c, VA ⇣ >1–2 lines, or ⍉healed after 72h → urgent ophthalmology
▪︎defect w/ infiltrate or ulcer → same-day ophthalmology
▪︎serious infect involving multi layers of the cornea
: eye pain, conjunctival inj, FB sensation, photophobia, lacrimation
round or irreg ulcer w/ white, hazy base
triangular, fibrovascular wedge of conjunctival tissue
